summary: Elevated TTFB for chat completions after routing/kernel rollout causing cold-compile path
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports elevated time-to-first-token (TTFB) for chat completions after nightly runtime + kernel selection rollout. Problem began shortly after changes to routing policy and kernel selection were deployed to production canaries and then gradually to the us-east serving pool.

Observed behaviour: High initial latency (TTFB) for first token on chat responses, sometimes followed by streaming disconnects. Some requests hit API timeouts (504) when the initial token emission exceeded internal proxies' deadline.

Reported by: BrightForms support contact after alerting from their monitoring and increased end-user complaints.
impact: Multiple production chat sessions for BrightForms experienced degraded UX; median TTFB increased from ~90ms to ~1.2s for affected routes, 95th percentile > 4.5s. ~8% of requests for the customer in us-east returned 504s over a 2 hour window. Business impact: user-facing session failures and customers escalated to enterprise SLA team.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use BrightForms production API key in us-east; send a chat completion with ~4 messages history + system prompt (~1.2k tokens total).
2) Observe response headers: X-Serving-Path, X-Kernel-Mode, X-Prefix-Cache (if present).
3) Repeat across several connection attempts; compare median TTFB across requests that hit nodes labeled 'kernel-new' vs 'kernel-stable'.
4) Variation: send identical request but pin model to redwood-open-7b-v2@2026-02-28 and note TTFB delta.
logs: Request IDs sampled: req-20260310-9a2f, req-20260310-9f4b, req-20260310-a12c
Serving logs: node=us-east-prod-rt-17 kernel_mode=new-kernel compile_path=warmup_started compile_time_ms=1320 stall_ms=1180
Proxy logs: proxy-1 | req=req-20260310-9a2f | upstream_latency=1250ms | response_code=504
investigation_notes: Initial triage (Support): Confirmed customer symptoms and gathered request IDs and timestamps. Escalated to SRE + Runtime team.

SRE observation: Regression coincides with rollout of kernel-selection change (PR #4321) that introduced a path which triggers an on-node kernel compile for certain operator shapes when matching a newly preferred kernel variant.
Telemetry: Canary metrics showed an increase in kernel compile events on routes with long context; compile events caused main inference thread to block for up to 1.2s on affected nodes.

Routing note: New routing policy prefers 'latency-optimized' kernel variant that for quantized weights falls back to on-host compile when operator tiling doesn't match cached kernels. This path didn't get sufficient canary coverage for long chat histories.

KV/prefix cache interaction: Requests with large context that would have matched a cached KV slot instead hit the cold path because cache key normalization changed in the same release; cache miss amplified compile exposure.

Customer repro: BrightForms able to reproduce with repeatable 600–1200ms initial stalls when their request landed on nodes with the new-kernel label. Pinning to older model or disabling routing preference reduced TTFB to baseline.

Hypothesis: combination of kernel-selection fallback + cache-key normalization change caused cache misses that exposed a previously rare compile code path, creating blocking stalls and proxy timeouts.
comments: 2026-03-10 10:14 Support (Marina): Collected sample request IDs and forwarded to SRE. Asked customer to pin to older model as temporary mitigation.
2026-03-10 10:40 SRE (Diego): Confirmed increased compile events on us-east nodes; spike coincides with rollout window 02:00-03:30 UTC. Investigating compiler_wrapper blocking behavior.

2026-03-10 11:05 Runtime Eng (Sophie Chen): Identified PR #4321 as the likely change, reproduced locally by forcing kernel preference to 'new-kernel' and running long-context traces. Submitted hotfix to skip compile on hotpath (PR draft).
2026-03-10 12:22 Support (Marina): Informed BrightForms of mitigation options (model pin, routing override). Customer applied model pin and reported immediate improvement for new sessions.
2026-03-11 03:01 SRE (Diego): Deployed emergency rollback of kernel-selection to canary-only; metrics returned to baseline for affected nodes. Rolling fix being validated.
2026-03-12 09:34 Runtime Eng (Sophie): Landed non-blocking compile patch and added extra cache-key normalization guards (PRs: 4330, 4333). Scheduling broad rollout after validation.
2026-03-13 16:00 Support (Marina): Customer confirmed degradation resolved for pinned routes and reported no further 504s after rollback/patch.
resolution: Temporary mitigation: advised customer to pin to redwood-open-7b-v2@2026-02-28 or disable the new routing preference for affected routes. Engineering rolled kernel-selection back to canary in us-east, which restored baseline TTFB. Permanent fix: landed non-blocking compile path and cache-key normalization patch; preparing safe rollout with extended canary for long-history chat traces. Follow-up actions: add high-cardinality telemetry for compile events, add explicit SLO guard that aborts compile-blocking path when proxy deadlines are near, and update rollout playbook to include long-history chat test cases.
next_steps: 1) Runtime team to complete full rollout of non-blocking compile patch with extended canary (owner: Sophie Chen, ETA: 2026-03-20).
2) SRE to add alert rule for kernel-compile events >300ms per node (owner: Diego Alvarez, ETA: 2026-03-15).
3) Support to follow up with BrightForms in 48 hours to confirm no regressions (owner: Marina Patel, ETA: 2026-03-15).
4) Create INT ticket to review rollout gating and include long-history prime tests (linked: INT-4042).
